Definition: from a compound of G575 and G756; a beginning of sacrifice, i.e. the (Jewish) first-fruit (figuratively):--first-fruits.
BiblicalUsage: The firstfruits are the first sheaf of the harvest, offered to God as a promise of the rest to come. Paul calls Christ the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep, and calls believers the firstfruits of God's creatures; Romans speaks of the firstfruits of the Spirit in us now, and Revelation sees the redeemed as firstfruits to God and the Lamb.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the firstfruits tell me the harvest is certain. Christ rose first, so those who belong to him will follow, and the Spirit already living in us is God's down payment on the day the whole harvest comes in.
